state: Finite slices of u64 weights; every position is a distinct symbol even when its weight is zero. Codes are vectors of booleans in original order. Successful allocation, ordinary usize<=64-bit platforms.
forward: Return deterministic binary prefix codes minimizing sum_i w_i*len(code_i) among prefix-free nonempty codes. Empty yields []; singleton yields [[false]]. Merge queue orders by (u128 subtree sum, creation index); false labels first pop, true second. New parents follow original indices.
inverse: Exclude wrong symbol count, empty code for any present symbol, duplicate or prefix-related codes, suboptimal weighted cost, and ties/orientations inconsistent with creation-order merging. Empty and singleton conventions are part of the exact behavior.

For an observed code forest C, compatible weights are all nonnegative u64 vectors whose ordered merge inequalities select its oriented tree under (sum,index) comparisons. Ties permit <= only when creation index wins. Positive scaling within u64 preserves comparisons, so recovery is generally nonunique; [1,1] and [5,9] both yield [false],[true].
cost: O(n log n + L) time, O(n+L) space where L is total emitted code length, up to O(n²). Sums in u128 cannot overflow for allocated u64 slices on <=64-bit usize. Weighted cost is measured in tests with u128.
